audit.evidence_class: Exploratory post-primary paired contrasts; original primary family unchanged
caveats: Difference between models is tested by paired gain differences, never inferred from differing significance
All intervals resample the same64 source pairs within domain; no independent model resampling
Conditional source bootstrap cannot remove shared-calendar dependence; median point outputs evaluated using MSE
Post-primary comparisons do not select new thresholds, depths or deployments

observations: One of six primary fixed-depth1 contrasts has a positive adjusted mean-gain interval: TimesFM electricity. MSE 0.5515747684009784 native versus 0.4676360158302627 hybrid1; paired gain 0.08393875257071565, family6 interval [0.015307078093565, 0.1583223135327461]. 24 wins, 5 losses, 35 abstention ties; 29/64 extraction-eligible.

Electricity seasonal24 MSE is 0.3993750427653811, lower than TimesFM hybrid1. Hybrid gain over seasonal is -0.06826097306488155, exploratory paired95 interval [-0.18320746836788693, 0.03347570035936674]. Improvement over native does not establish superiority over seasonal.

Electricity paired difference of hybrid gains, TimesFM minus Bolt, is 0.08759837877876678 with exploratory paired95 interval [0.03636936339632568, 0.14299372586476694]. M4 and traffic between-model paired intervals include zero. No between-model claim is inferred from differing significance.

Both traffic fixed hybrids worsen MSE, with negative adjusted primary intervals. The frozen selector avoids most traffic harm but its mean gain remains slightly negative for both models. No general hybrid deployment is supported.

Continuous two-hindcast/main rank association is positive after diagnostic Holm6 for Bolt M4 and both traffic models. Electricity associations are near zero overall. These are source-level retrospective associations with temporal and calendar-dependence caveats, not learned future thresholds.

The original pilot secondary rules, seasonal and tone-last controls, all source records, conditional eligibility summaries and full forecasts remain available; no TEST-selected depth or threshold was deployed.

caveats: Difference between models is tested by paired gain differences, never inferred from differing significance

Conditional source bootstrap cannot remove shared-calendar dependence; median point outputs evaluated using MSE

observations: One of six primary fixed-depth1 contrasts has a positive adjusted mean-gain interval: TimesFM electricity. MSE 0.5515747684009784 native versus 0.4676360158302627 hybrid1; paired gain 0.08393875257071565, family6 interval [0.015307078093565, 0.1583223135327461]. 24 wins, 5 losses, 35 abstention ties; 29/64 extraction-eligible.

Electricity seasonal24 MSE is 0.3993750427653811, lower than TimesFM hybrid1. Hybrid gain over seasonal is -0.06826097306488155, exploratory paired95 interval [-0.18320746836788693, 0.03347570035936674]. Improvement over native does not establish superiority over seasonal.

Electricity paired difference of hybrid gains, TimesFM minus Bolt, is 0.08759837877876678 with exploratory paired95 interval [0.03636936339632568, 0.14299372586476694]. M4 and traffic between-model paired intervals include zero. No between-model claim is inferred from differing significance.

Both traffic fixed hybrids worsen MSE, with negative adjusted primary intervals. The frozen selector avoids most traffic harm but its mean gain remains slightly negative for both models. No general hybrid deployment is supported.

Continuous two-hindcast/main rank association is positive after diagnostic Holm6 for Bolt M4 and both traffic models. Electricity associations are near zero overall. These are source-level retrospective associations with temporal and calendar-dependence caveats, not learned future thresholds.

The original pilot secondary rules, seasonal and tone-last controls, all source records, conditional eligibility summaries and full forecasts remain available; no TEST-selected depth or threshold was deployed.
